terra.problem: The verse does not say who whispers in the disciples’ ears; the explanation attributes the whisper to Jesus.
It assumes why the baker chose voice, though the baker has not given a reason.
The claim that sparrows were among the cheapest things in the market adds a historical fact the passage does not give.
The sparrow at Papa Dorin’s windowsill adds an animal to his world, beyond the established backstory.
The two-sparrow price is mentioned two verses earlier, not one.
Jesus begins the verse with “So do not be afraid,” rather than ending with it.
“That’s not what I expected to read either” assumes the baker shared Papa Dorin’s expectation.
The joke about a staff being easier on the hands makes light of the cross’s suffering.
The forgotten-timer joke repeats the timer-and-forgetting idea from stop 1, card 2, answer 3.
Saying that receiving the prophet earns the reward adds a claim about earning that the text does not make.
The explanation states the reward is for giving water to a disciple without the verse’s condition that it is given because he is Jesus’ disciple.
The explanation omits both the recipient and the reason for giving, making the promise sound as though it applies to any giver of a cup of water.
The explanation is a flat, mechanical restatement of the verse, with little of Papa Dorin’s personality in a moment that could carry it.
